ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: The Art of Levity: Interpreting British and American Visual Humor. How does visual humor differ from literary or oral humor? What constitutes a visual joke? What techniques do paintings, comic strips, or film sequences mobilize in their efforts to draw a laugh? How are jokes recycled or revised according to different media or cultural contexts? This course addresses these and other questions by focusing on comic production in England and the United States. We will look primarily at the nineteenth century, but our discussions will necessarily draw us into the humor of our own time, as we examine a range of visual material: from single-sheet cartoons to architectural ornament, from the popular press to popular film. We will consider this material in the context of social and political attitudes, styles of communication, consumer culture, aesthetic theory, and humor theory more generally. Graduate Section.
